payload.claim: No test ever calls `create_run` with a non-`None` `batch_id`; every new test (`test_a_run_created_outside_a_batch_has_a_null_batch_id`, `test_a_ledger_built_by_the_previous_schema_still_opens_and_writes`) only exercises the default-`None` path. Replacing the tuple `(repo_id, base_sha, batch_id)` at this INSERT with `(repo_id, base_sha, None)` — i.e. silently discarding the caller's `batch_id` argument entirely — would keep every test in this diff green while defeating the entire reason the parameter and column exist (grouping a run into the batch that ran it, per §4.2.1). The suite's own `test_a_batch_status_outside_the_four_stop_reasons_is_rejected` shows raw `batches` rows can already be inserted via `ledger._db` in a test, so a counterpart asserting a real `batch_id` round-trips through `create_run` was reachable but wasn't written.
